# `tfctl profile`

The `tfctl profile` command provides subcommands for managing profile settings.

## Usage

```shell-session
$ tfctl profile <subcommand> [options]
```

## Description

The `tfctl profile` command group provides subcommands to manage the active profile's settings. Use these commands to view and modify properties such as the default organization, hostname, and authentication token for the currently active profile.

Profiles are useful when you need to manage multiple organizations or work across different instances of HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise. Each profile stores its own configuration, allowing you to switch contexts without reconfiguring tfctl. To learn how to manage profiles, refer to [Manage tfctl profiles](/terraform/tfctl-cli/profiles).

## Command groups

- [`profiles`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/profile/profiles) - Manage configuration profiles

## Subcommands

- [`display`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/profile/display) - Display properties for the active profile
- [`get`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/profile/get) - Get a property value for the active profile
- [`set`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/profile/set) - Set a property value for the active profile
- [`unset`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/profile/unset) - Unset a property for the active profile

## Available properties

You can configure the following properties for each profile:

- `default_organization`: Default organization. When you use `tfctl api` with paths containing `{organization}` placeholders, tfctl uses this value automatically when you omit an organization using `-p organization=VALUE` for supported commands.
- `hostname`: HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise hostname
- `name`: Profile name
- `no_color`: If `true`, tfctl does not use color when it prints messages to stdout
- `telemetry`: Specifies whether telemetry is enabled and if tfctl writes the output to its log. You can specify `enabled`, `disabled`, or `log`.
- `token`: The API token to use for all requests in plain text.

## Examples

The following command displays all profile settings:

```shell-session
$ tfctl profile display
```

The following command sets the default organization:

```shell-session
$ tfctl profile set default_organization my-org
```
